chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Abdullah ibn Bahr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the performer of Tamattu' who fasted three days during the Hajj, then he found/afforded a sacrificial animal (had) on the day he exited from Mina. He (peace be upon him) said: 'His fasting suffices him.'

key_terms.أَجْزَأَهُ: It suffices him / is accepted for him
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٍ: A pilgrim who performs Umrah and Hajj separately, offering a sacrifice

ai.seo_question: Does fasting three days suffice if a pilgrim later affords the sacrificial animal?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that the three-day fast serves as a complete substitute for the sacrificial animal in Tamattu' Hajj, even if the pilgrim's financial capacity improves later. This ruling underscores the principle of ease (taysir) in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring that the obligation is fulfilled by the act performed at the time of inability, without requiring redundant compensation. It highlights the flexibility of the fidya (expiation) mechanism, prioritizing the pilgrim's actual capability at the moment of obligation.
